### Auxiliary subroutines

Subroutine DBCHK is used to see if debug output should be written to the output file.

Subroutine ESPREP is used to set the default site preparation probabilities (none, mechanical, and burn)

Subroutine ESRANN is used to generate random numbers in the regeneration establishment extension.

ESRNSD, an entry point in subroutine ESRANN, is used to reseed the random number generator in the regeneration establishment extension.

Subroutine ESTIME is used to calculate the time interval between the tally year and the year of disturbance, or site preparation, or the beginning of the current tally.

Subroutine MYOPEN is used to open an external file to be used for regeneration information.

OPDEL1, an entry point in subroutine OPFIND, is used to delete an activity scheduled for the projection cycle.

OPDONE, an entry point in subroutine OPFIND, is used to set the year an activity is accomplished.

Subroutine OPFIND is used to find any regeneration related activities scheduled for the projection cycle.

OPGET, an entry point in subroutine OPFIND, is used to retrieve activities and related parameters scheduled for the projection cycle to the subroutine that will process them.

OPGETC, an entry point in subroutine OPFIND, is used to retrieve a character string associated with an activity.

Subroutine OPRDAT is used to read a file containing activities that need to be scheduled for the current stand.

Subroutine SPESRT is used to reset the species order sort of tree records.

## Computing crown ratio change and crown width {#sec-computing-crown-ratio-change-and-crown-width}

Change in a tree’s crown ratio and a tree’s crown width are the last tree attributes to be estimated during a growth projection cycle. A tree’s crown ratio may decrease, stay the same, or increase. The change of a cycle is limited to 1 percent of the tree’s crown ratio per year of the cycle in all variants except AK, where the limit on an increase is 3 percent per year, and the new crown ratio is also limited to the value that the height growth of the cycle allows in most variants, as described below.

### Subroutines involved and their function

**Crown ratio change.** Subroutine CROWN estimates the crown ratio of each tree at the end of the cycle. Subroutine GRADD calls CROWN after subroutine UPDATE, so DBH(i) and HT(i) are already the end-of-cycle values when CROWN is called, and DG(i) and HTG(i) still hold the increments of the cycle. Crown ratio is carried as the integer percent ICR(i). The steps are the same in every variant, except as noted; the variables are defined in the next table.

```{r crown-change-variables, echo=FALSE}
crown_change_variables <- tibble::tribble(
  ~Variable, ~Definition, ~Units,
  "ICR", "Crown ratio of the tree at the start of the cycle, as an integer percent", "percent",
  "CRNEW", "Crown ratio of the tree from the crown ratio model", "percent",
  "CHG", "Change in crown ratio of the cycle", "percent",
  "FINT", "Length of the projection cycle", "years",
  "PDIFPY", "Relative change per year, CHG / ICR / FINT", "per year",
  "CRNMLT", "Crown ratio multiplier of the species from the CRNMULT keyword (1.0 when no multiplier is given)", "ratio",
  "DLOW, DHI", "Lower and upper limits of DBH of the CRNMULT keyword (defaults 0 and 99.0)", "inches",
  "HT, HTG", "Total height after the update, and height increment of the cycle", "feet",
  "CRMAX", "Largest crown ratio that the height growth allows", "percent",
  "HF", "Height at the end of the cycle used by the crown length equations, HT + HTG", "feet",
  "DF", "Diameter at the end of the cycle used by the CR variant, DBH + DG / BARK", "inches",
  "BA", "Stand basal area", "square feet per acre",
  "RELDEN", "Stand crown competition factor", "percent",
  "SDIAC, SDIDEF", "Stand SDI, and the maximum SDI of the species", "trees per acre",
  "RELSDI", "Relative density, SDIAC / SDIDEF (1.0 when SDIDEF is not positive), with a maximum of 1.5", "ratio",
  "ISORT", "Rank of the tree in the diameter distribution of the stand, 1 for the smallest and ITRN for the largest", "rank",
  "PCT", "Percentile of the tree in the basal area distribution of the stand", "percent"
)

kable(crown_change_variables,
      col.names = c("Variable", "Definition", "Units"),
      caption = "Variables used in the crown ratio change equations",
      booktabs = TRUE) %>%
  kable_styling(bootstrap_options = c("striped", "hover", "condensed"),
                full_width = FALSE, font_size = 9) %>%
  column_spec(1, bold = TRUE, width = "6em") %>%
  column_spec(2, width = "34em")
```

For each tree record, CROWN does the following.

1. If ICR(i) is negative, the crown ratio change was calculated by an extension that kills or damages crown (the top-kill option HTGSTOP of subroutine HTGSTP, the fire and fuels extension, the western spruce budworm and tussock moth extensions). CROWN changes the sign of ICR(i) and makes no other change. (KT, EM species LL and IE species of the NI form test for ICR(i) greater than 0, so a record with a crown ratio of 0 is also left unchanged in those variants.)
2. The crown ratio of the model, CRNEW, is calculated with the equation of the species and variant (see the table that follows the equations).
3. The change, CHG = CRNEW - ICR, is limited to 1 percent of ICR per year of the cycle, as shown in equation {4.8.1.1}. The limit applies to a decrease as well as to an increase. In AK the limit on an increase is 3 percent per year.
4. If DLOW is not more than DBH(i) and DBH(i) is not more than DHI, the new value is ICR + CHG x CRNMLT; otherwise it is ICR + CHG. ICRI is this value rounded to an integer.
5. ICRI is limited by CRMAX, calculated with equation {4.8.1.2}. If ICRI is less than 10 and CRNMLT is 1.0, ICRI is set to CRMAX.
6. ICRI is limited to a maximum of 95 and, when CRNMLT is 1.0, to a minimum of 10, and to a minimum of 1.

$$
\begin{aligned}
CHG &= \begin{cases} 0.01 \cdot ICR \cdot FINT & \text{if } PDIFPY > 0.01 \\ -0.01 \cdot ICR \cdot FINT & \text{if } PDIFPY < -0.01 \\ CRNEW - ICR & \text{otherwise} \end{cases} \\
PDIFPY &= \frac{CRNEW - ICR}{ICR \cdot FINT}
\end{aligned}
\tag{4.8.1.1}
$$

Where:

- CHG: Change in crown ratio of the cycle (percent); the limit is a fraction of the crown ratio at the start of the cycle (for example, ICR of 50 and FINT of 10 years allow a change of 5 percentage points)
- ICR: Crown ratio of the tree at the start of the cycle, as an integer percent (percent)
- CRNEW: Crown ratio of the tree from the crown ratio model (percent)
- FINT: Length of the projection cycle (years)

$$
CRMAX = \frac{CRLN + HTG}{HT + HTG} \times 100, \qquad CRLN = \frac{HT \cdot ICR}{100}
\tag{4.8.1.2}
$$

Where:

- CRMAX: Largest crown ratio that the height growth allows (percent)
- HT: Total height of the tree (feet); the value is the height after the update
- HTG: Height increment of the cycle (feet)
- ICR: Crown ratio of the tree at the start of the cycle (percent)

The height growth limit of equation {4.8.1.2} is not applied in the NI-type model of KT, BC, EM species LL and the NI-type species of IE, where the height of the tree enters the equation. In OC and OP it is applied to the ORGANON trees. HT in equation {4.8.1.2} is the height after the update, so the equation adds HTG to a height that already includes it. The same applies to HF in the crown length equations, where HF = HT + HTG.

**Variants and models.** Six model forms are used in the code. The variant and species that use each form are given in the table that follows the equations.

$$
\begin{aligned}
ACRNEW &= C0 + C1 \cdot RELSDI \cdot 100 \\
A &= WEIBA, \qquad B = WEIBB0 + WEIBB1 \cdot ACRNEW, \qquad C = WEIBC0 + WEIBC1 \cdot ACRNEW \\
X &= \min\left[0.95, \; \max\left(0.05, \; SCALE \cdot \frac{ISORT}{ITRN}\right)\right] \\
CRNEW &= 10\left[A + B\left(-\ln(1 - X)\right)^{1/C}\right]
\end{aligned}
\tag{4.8.1.3}
$$

Where:

- C0, C1, WEIBA, WEIBB0, WEIBB1, WEIBC0, WEIBC1: Coefficients of the species (arrays of the same names in subroutine CROWN)
- SCALE: Density scale, with the forms of equation {4.8.1.4}
- CRNEW: Crown ratio of the model (percent); the factor 10 converts the Weibull value in tenths to percent
- RELSDI: Relative density, SDIAC / SDIDEF (1.0 when SDIDEF is not positive), with a maximum of 1.5
- ISORT: Rank of the tree in the diameter distribution of the stand, 1 for the smallest and ITRN for the largest
- ITRN: Number of tree records

B is at least 1.0 or 3.0, as stated in the table, and C is at least 2.0. The quantile X is smallest for the smallest tree.

$$
\begin{aligned}
SCALE_1 &= 1 - 0.00167\,(RELDEN - 100) \\
SCALE_2 &= 1.5 - RELSDI \\
SCALE_3 &= 1 - 0.00333\,(RELDEN - 50)
\end{aligned}
\qquad (0.30 \le SCALE \le 1.0)
\tag{4.8.1.4}
$$

Where:

- SCALE: Density scale; the form used by each variant is given in the table
- RELDEN: Stand crown competition factor (percent)
- RELSDI: Relative density, SDIAC / SDIDEF (1.0 when SDIDEF is not positive), with a maximum of 1.5

SCALE form 1 is used in the variants shown with that form in the table, and SCALE form 2 in CA, NC and OC. In WS, SCALE_2 is used for species LP, WB, PM, KP, FP, CP, LM, GP, WE, WJ, UJ, CJ, SCALE_3 for species SP, DF, WF, GS, IC, JP, RF, PP, WP, SF, MP, BD, RW, MH, LO, CY, BL, BO, VO, IO, TO, GC, AS, CL, MA, DG, BM, OS, OH, and SCALE_1 for species MC. The same Weibull form is used for dubbing missing crown ratios, as described in [Dub missing crown ratios](#sec-model-calibration-and-other-setup-tasks).

In SN, the Weibull parameters are WEIBUL(1) for A, WEIBUL(2) + WEIBUL(3) x ACRNEW for B, and WEIBUL(4) for C, and the Weibull value is already in percent, so CRNEW = A + B x (-ln(1 - X))^(1/C), without the factor 10. RELSDI = SDIAC / SDIDEF x 10 with a value of 6.0 when SDIDEF is not positive, bounded to 1 to 12. The mean crown ratio of the species is calculated with one of five forms, selected by the first element of the array MCREQN of the species, as shown in equation {4.8.1.5}; the coefficients a, b and c of the equation are elements of the array MCREQN of the species, as listed below.

$$
ACRNEW =
\begin{cases}
\exp\left(a + b \ln(RELSDI) + c \cdot RELSDI\right) & \text{form 1 (Hoerl)} \\
\exp\left(a + b \ln(RELSDI)\right) & \text{form 2 (power)} \\
a + c \cdot RELSDI & \text{form 3 (linear)} \\
a + b \log_{10}(RELSDI) & \text{form 4 (logarithmic)} \\
\dfrac{RELSDI}{a \cdot RELSDI + b} & \text{form 5 (inverse)}
\end{cases}
\tag{4.8.1.5}
$$

Where:

- a: MCREQN(2); b: MCREQN(4) in forms 1 and 2, MCREQN(5) in form 4, MCREQN(6) in form 5; c: MCREQN(3) in forms 1 and 3 (the coefficients in the source are named AMCR, BMCR and CMCR)
- RELSDI: Relative density, bounded 1 to 12
- ACRNEW: Mean crown ratio of the stand for the species (percent)

$$
CRNEW = 100 \cdot \frac{CL}{HF}, \qquad CL = \min\left[HF, \; \max\left(1, \; CL_0\right)\right], \qquad CL_0 =
\begin{cases}
5.17281 + 0.32552 \cdot HF - 0.01675 \cdot BA & \text{CR-type} \\
-0.59373 + 0.67703 \cdot HF & \text{PI/JU-type}
\end{cases}
\tag{4.8.1.6}
$$

Where:

- HF: HT + HTG (feet)
- BA: Stand basal area (square feet per acre)
- CRNEW: Crown ratio of the tree at the end of the cycle (percent)

In equation {4.8.1.6} the crown ratio does not depend on the previous crown ratio of the tree except through the limits of equation {4.8.1.1}.

$$
\begin{aligned}
X &= B_1 + B_2 \ln\left(\frac{12\, HT}{DBH}\right) + B_3 \cdot PRD + B_4 \,\frac{DBH}{QMDPLT} \\
CRNEW &= 100 \cdot \min\left[0.95, \; \max\left(0.05, \; \frac{1}{1 + e^{X}}\right)\right]
\end{aligned}
\tag{4.8.1.7}
$$

Where:

- B1 to B4: Coefficients of the species (the arrays CRINT, CRHDR, CRRD and CRDQMD in AK); in the redwood equations of the other variants, B1 is -1.021064, B2 is 0.309296, B3 is 0.869720 and B4 is -0.116274
- PRD: Relative density of the point where the tree is located: the Zeide relative density of the point divided by the maximum SDI of the point, and 0 when the maximum SDI of the point is not positive
- QMDPLT: Quadratic mean diameter of the point, sqrt(PTBAA / PTPA / 0.005454) (inches), with a minimum of 1.0
- HT: Total height of the tree after the update (feet); 12 x HT / DBH is the height-diameter ratio, HDR
- DBH: Diameter at breast height (inches)
- CRNEW: Crown ratio of the tree at the end of the cycle (percent)

$$
\begin{aligned}
CRNEW &= 10\left[\frac{BCR1}{1 + BCR2 \cdot BA} + BCR3\left(1 - \exp(-BCR4 \cdot DBH)\right)\right]
\end{aligned}
\tag{4.8.1.8}
$$

Where:

- BCR1 to BCR4: Coefficients of the species (arrays of the same names); in LS, NE and ON the equation is written with exp(BCR4 x DBH) and the coefficient BCR4 has the opposite sign
- BA: Stand basal area (square feet per acre)
- DBH: Diameter at breast height (inches)
- CRNEW: Crown ratio of the tree at the end of the cycle (percent)

$$
\begin{aligned}
PCR &= CRCON + P_1 BA + P_2 BA^{2} + P_3 \ln(BA) + P_4 RELDEN + P_5 RELDEN^{2} + P_6 \ln(RELDEN) \\
&\quad + B_7 DBH + B_8 DBH^{2} + B_9 \ln(DBH) + B_{10} HT + B_{11} HT^{2} + B_{12} \ln(HT) + B_{13}\, PCT + B_{14} \ln(PCT) \\
CHG &= \exp(PCR_{end}) - \exp(PCR_{start}), \qquad ICRI = ICR + CRNMLT \cdot CHG \cdot 100 + 0.50005
\end{aligned}
\tag{4.8.1.9}
$$

Where:

- CRCON: Constant of the species and habitat type (array CRCON)
- P1 to P6, B7 to B14: Coefficients of the species (the array PARM; B7 to B14 are PARM(ISPC,7) to PARM(ISPC,14))
- PCR(end): PCR with the attributes at the end of the cycle
- PCR(start): PCR with the attributes at the start of the cycle: DBH - DG / BARK, HT - HTG, PCT of the previous cycle (OLDPCT, or the present PCT when the stand was thinned), and the stand BA and RELDEN of the previous cycle (when the CCF of the previous cycle was less than 100, the present BA and RELDEN)
- PCT: Percentile of the tree in the basal area distribution, with a minimum of 0.01
- BA: Stand basal area (square feet per acre)
- RELDEN: Stand crown competition factor (percent)
- DBH: Diameter at breast height (inches)
- HT: Total height after the update (feet)
- ICR: Crown ratio of the tree at the start of the cycle (percent)
- CRNMLT: Crown ratio multiplier of the species from the CRNMULT keyword (1.0 when no multiplier is given)
- CHG: Change in crown ratio of the cycle, a proportion in the NI-type model
- ICRI: Crown ratio of the tree after the change, rounded to an integer (percent), before the limits of CROWN are applied

In the NI-type model CHG is a proportion; it is limited to 1 percent of ICR per year (equation {4.8.1.1}, with CHG and ICR in the same units). In KT the minimum crown ratio is 5 (when CRNMLT is 1.0), and there is no minimum of 10 and no height growth limit (CRMAX). A random draw, BACHLO(CR, CRSD) with CRSD of 6.35, replaces the value only when missing crown ratios are dubbed with DGSD of 1.0 or more; it is not used in the cycles. A tree smaller than 3.0 inches at the start of the cycle (DBH - DG / BARK) in KT, EM (species LL) and IE (NI-type species) keeps its crown ratio; subroutine REGENT dubs the crown ratio when the tree reaches 3.0 inches.

```{r crown-by-variant, echo=FALSE}
kable(crown_by_variant,
      col.names = c("Variant", "Species", "Model", "Arrays and source"),

      booktabs = TRUE) %>%
  kable_styling(bootstrap_options = c("striped", "hover", "condensed"),
```

In the variants that use a diameter rank (equation {4.8.1.3}), a tree with a diameter of zero would use a random number for X; this branch is not reached for trees with a diameter. The threshold diameter of 1.0 inch in the source applies only when missing crown ratios are dubbed. In the variants other than KT, BC, EM (species LL) and IE (NI-type species) the change is calculated for every tree during the cycles, and in SN, CR, CS, LS, NE and ON there is no threshold diameter in the source at all.

**Crown ratio change in the BC variant when LV2ATV is false.** Subroutine CRNMD evaluates, at the start and at the end of the cycle, YCR = CON + CRHTDBH x (H / D) + CRHT x H + CRDBH2 x D^2 + CRBAL x BAL, where H is the height in meters, D is the diameter in centimeters (a diameter below 2 cm is replaced by 2 cm, with the height of a tree of that diameter), BAL is the basal area in larger trees in square meters per hectare, and CON is the constant of the species built from the biogeoclimatic zone, elevation, slope and aspect. YCR is limited to the range -9.21 to 9.21, and the crown ratio is 1 / (1 + exp(YCR)). The change is the difference of the two crown ratios, and it is limited as in equation {4.8.1.1} (`canada/bc/crown.f` lines 730 to 779).

**Crown ratio change in the CR variant.** CROWN calls subroutine GEMCR with the end-of-cycle height, HF = HT + HTG, and diameter, DF = DBH + DG / BARK (at least DBH). GEMCR returns the crown length, CL, with an equation of the species and model type of the stand (1, southwest mixed conifer; 2, southwest ponderosa pine; 3, Black Hills ponderosa pine; 4, spruce-fir; 5, lodgepole pine), and CRNEW = 100 x CL / HF with the bounds of equation {4.8.1.6}, except for species MH, RC and WL, for which GEMCR returns the crown ratio directly. The equations are given in the next table, where BA is the stand basal area, BAU is the basal area in the diameter classes larger than the class of the tree, PCTI is PCT, and DF and HF are as above.

```{r crown-gemcr, echo=FALSE}
crown_gemcr <- tibble::tribble(
  ~Species, ~Model_Type, ~Equation,
  "AF, CB", "1, 2", "CL = 0.50706 + 0.73070 x HF",
  "AF, CB", "3, 4, 5", "CL = 0.36135 + 0.57085 x HF",

  "GF, WF", "All", "CL = 6.22959 + 0.67587 x HF - 0.03098 x BA",
  "MH", "All", "CR = 0.3450 - 0.00264 x BA + 0.00000512 x RELDEN^2 - 0.25138 x ln(H) + 0.05140 x ln(PCTI) (crown ratio directly)",
  "RC", "All", "CR = -1.6053 + 0.17479 x ln(BA) - 0.00183 x RELDEN - 0.00560 x DF + 0.11050 x ln(PCTI) (crown ratio directly)",
  "WL", "All", "CR = 0.03441 - 0.00204 x BA + 0.30066 x ln(DF) - 0.59302 x ln(H) (crown ratio directly)",
  "LP", "All", "CL = 5.00215 + 0.06334 x HF + 0.88236 x DF - 0.03821 x BAU",
  "BC, LM, PI, WB, UJ, GO, AW, EM, BK, SO, AJ, RM, OJ, ER, PM, PD, AZ, OS", "All", "CL = -0.59373 + 0.67703 x HF (equation {4.8.1.6}, PI/JU-type)",
  "PP, CI", "1", "CL = 5.63367 + 0.56252 x HF - 0.06411 x BA",
  "PP, CI", "2", "CL = 4.35671 + 0.84714 x DF + 0.32549 x HF - 0.03802 x BA",
  "PP, CI", "3, 4, 5", "CL = 3.49178 + 0.80767 x DF + 0.17421 x HF - 0.03272 x BA",
  "SW", "All", "CL = 3.03832 + 0.65587 x HF - 0.01792 x BA",
  "BS", "All", "CL = 3.61635 + 0.93639 x DF + 0.61547 x HF - 0.02360 x BA",
  "ES", "1, 2", "CL = 1.05857 + 0.68442 x HF",
  "ES", "3, 4, 5", "CL = 3.22244 + 0.44315 x HF + 0.44755 x DF",
  "WS", "All", "CL = 0.15768 + 0.74697 x HF",

kable(crown_gemcr,
      col.names = c("Species", "Model type", "Equation of subroutine GEMCR"),
      caption = "Crown length and crown ratio equations of the CR variant",
      booktabs = TRUE) %>%
  kable_styling(bootstrap_options = c("striped", "hover", "condensed"),
                full_width = FALSE, font_size = 9) %>%
  column_spec(1, bold = TRUE, width = "7em") %>%
  column_spec(3, width = "34em")
```

**ORGANON trees in OC and OP.** For a valid ORGANON tree (LORGANON is true and IORG(i) is 1), CRNEW is the end-of-cycle crown ratio of ORGANON, ANINT(100 x CR2(i)), from subroutine EXECUTE, which is called from subroutine DGDRIV. The limit of equation {4.8.1.1} is not applied to these trees; CHG = CRNEW - ICR is multiplied by CRNMLT in the DBH range of the CRNMULT keyword, and CRMAX of equation {4.8.1.2} still applies. All other trees use the models of the table.

**The CRNMULT keyword.** The fields of the keyword are the date, the species (or species group or ALL), the multiplier (default 1.0), the lower DBH limit (default 0), the upper DBH limit (default 99.0), and a flag that applies the multiplier to the dubbed crown ratios only when it is greater than 0. When missing crown ratios are dubbed, or when a tree has no crown ratio, the dubbed value is multiplied by the multiplier, ICRI = INT(ICRI x CRNMLT), for trees in the DBH range. Because the minimum of 10 and the replacement of a crown ratio below 10 by CRMAX apply only when CRNMLT is 1.0, a multiplier other than 1.0 removes those two rules.

Once the end-of-cycle crown ratios have been estimated for all trees, program control returns to subroutine GRADD.

**Crown width.** Subroutine CWIDTH sets the crown width, CRWDTH(i) in feet, of every tree record. Subroutine GRADD calls it after subroutine CROWN, using the updated crown ratios, and subroutine FVS calls it once at the start of the projection (after subroutine CRATET) to give the initial crown widths. Regeneration and sprout records get their crown width from direct calls to subroutine CWCALC in the establishment and sprouting routines. CWIDTH has two loops of the same logic, one over the live tree records and one over the dead tree records of the first cycle (the records IREC2 to MAXTRE). Tripled records receive the crown width of the original record (subroutine TRIPLE). For each record, CWIDTH does the following.

1. If the user supplied crown width coefficients for the species (keyword CWEQN), CW = CWDS0 + CWDS1 x DBH + CWDS2 x DBH^CWDS3 when DBH is less than the transition diameter CWTDBH of the species, and CW = CWDL0 + CWDL1 x DBH + CWDL2 x DBH^CWDL3 otherwise (equation {4.8.1.10}).
2. Otherwise, CWIDTH calls subroutine CWCALC with the species, the tree diameter, height and crown ratio, and IWHO of 0 (forest-grown crown width).
3. CRWDTH(i) = CW. CWIDTH applies no bounds to the user-supplied equation; the default equations are bounded in CWCALC.
4. After the loops, each FIXCW activity of the cycle multiplies CRWDTH(i) by its multiplier for the records of the species (or species group, or all species) with a DBH that is at least the lower limit and less than the upper limit, and limits CRWDTH(i) to 99.9 feet. Because CWIDTH calculates the crown width again at each call, the multiplier is not cumulative.

$$
CW =
\begin{cases}
C0_S + C1_S \cdot DBH + C2_S \cdot DBH^{C3_S} & DBH < TC \\
C0_L + C1_L \cdot DBH + C2_L \cdot DBH^{C3_L} & DBH \ge TC
\end{cases}
\tag{4.8.1.10}
$$

Where:

- CW: Crown width (feet)
- DBH: Diameter at breast height (inches)
- TC: Transition diameter, CWTDBH, the second field of the CWEQN keyword record (inches)
- C0_S to C3_S: Coefficients CWDS0 to CWDS3, the first four values of the supplemental record of the keyword
- C0_L to C3_L: Coefficients CWDL0 to CWDL3, the last four values of the supplemental record of the keyword

The fields of the CWEQN keyword record are the species (or species group, or ALL) and TC; the supplemental record holds the eight coefficients (format 8F10.0). The fields of the FIXCW keyword record are the date or cycle, the species, the multiplier (default 1.0), the lower DBH limit (default 0, inclusive) and the upper DBH limit (default 999, exclusive). In the metric variants (BC and ON) CWIDTH is in `metric/base/cwidth.f`; user equations are evaluated in centimeters and meters and CRWDTH is converted to feet, and the FIXCW diameter limits are in centimeters.

**Crown width equations (subroutine CWCALC).** CWCALC is compiled from four files. The argument list is the same in all of them (species, trees per acre, diameter, height, crown ratio, integer crown ratio, crown width, IWHO).

```{r cwcalc-files, echo=FALSE}
cwcalc_files <- tibble::tribble(
  ~Source_File, ~Variants,
  "vie/cwcalc.f", "AK, BC, BM, CA, CI, CR, EC, EM, IE, KT, NC, OC, OP, PN, SO, TT, UT, WC, WS",
  "hi/cwcalc.f", "HI",
  "ls/cwcalc.f", "CS, LS, NE, SN",
  "canada/on/cwcalc.f", "ON"
)

kable(cwcalc_files,
      col.names = c("Source file", "Variants"),
      caption = "Source files of subroutine CWCALC",
      booktabs = TRUE) %>%
  kable_styling(bootstrap_options = c("striped", "hover", "condensed"),
                full_width = FALSE, font_size = 9)
```

In every file the crown width is bounded to at least 0.5 feet and at most 99.9 feet, and the equations carry a species-specific upper bound (examples are 16, 29, 33, 40 and 50 feet). For diameters below a minimum diameter the equations are scaled linearly: CW(D) = CW(D_min) x (D / D_min), where D_min is MIND (5.0 inches) for the Bechtold equations and OMIND for the others (1.0 inch in the western file and 3.0 inches in the eastern file). The equation of a species is identified by a five-character code: the three-digit FIA species code, and the two-digit equation number. The western file maps the species sequence number of the variant to this code (a DATA array for each variant); the eastern file maps the first two characters of the alpha species code to the code, and chooses the equation for open-grown crown width (IWHO = 1) where one exists. The equation numbers have different meanings in the two files. HI sets the variant code to PN and uses the PN map extended to its 45 species.

*Western equations (`vie/cwcalc.f` and `hi/cwcalc.f`).* The variables are DBH (inches), H (feet), CR (percent), CL = CR x H / 100 (crown length, feet), BAREA (stand basal area, with a minimum of 1.0), EL (elevation in hundreds of feet, limited to a range by species), HI (the Hopkins index = ((100 x ELEV - 5449) / 100) + (LAT - 42.16) x 4.0 + (-116.39 - LONG) x 1.25, limited to a range by species), and BF (a multiplier of the Crookston R6 model 2 equations for the national forest, and 1.0 for the other forests). The equation forms are written once in equation {4.8.1.11}.

$$
\begin{aligned}
\text{01 (Bechtold model 1):} \quad & CW = a + b\, D + c\, D^{2} \\
\text{02 (Bechtold model 2):} \quad & CW = a + b\, D \;[+\, c\, D^{2}] \;[+\, d\, CR] \;[+\, e\, HI] \\
\text{03 (Crookston, R1):} \quad & CW = k \exp\left(a + b \ln(CL) + c \ln(D)\right) \\
\text{04 (Crookston, R6, model 1):} \quad & CW = a\, D^{b} \\
\text{05 (Crookston, R6, model 2):} \quad & CW = a \cdot BF \cdot D^{b} H^{c} CL^{d} (BAREA + 1)^{e} \left(e^{EL}\right)^{f} \\
\text{06 (Donnelly, R6):} \quad & CW = a\, D^{b} \\
\text{08 (Castle, AK):} \quad & CW = a\, D^{b} H^{c} CL^{d} \;[(BAREA + 1)^{e} \left(e^{EL}\right)^{f}]
\end{aligned}
\tag{4.8.1.11}
$$

Where:

- CW: Crown width (feet)
- a to f, k: Coefficients of the species and equation (constants in the CASE of the equation code in the source file)
- D: Diameter at breast height (inches); equations 01 and 02 use MIND (5.0 inches) as the minimum diameter, equations 04, 05 and 06 use OMIND (1.0 inch), equation 03 uses 1.0 inch, and equation 08 gives 0.5 foot below 0.1 inch
- H: Total tree height (feet)
- CR: Crown ratio (percent)
- CL: Crown length, CR x H / 100 (feet)
- BAREA: Stand basal area, with a minimum of 1.0 (square feet per acre)
- EL: Elevation in hundreds of feet, limited to a range by species
- HI: Hopkins index of the western equations, defined in the text above
- BF: Multiplier of the Crookston R6 model 2 equations for the national forest, and 1.0 for the other forests

Terms in brackets are included only for some species; model 05 has the terms of BAREA and EL, H, or CL omitted for some species (the 5-character case shows the terms). Equation 07 (Moeur) is coded but is not assigned to any species.

For example, equation 01 of species 066 is CW = 2.1431 + 1.3447 x D - 0.0228 x D^2 (cap 29 feet), and equation 05 of species 122 is CW = 4.7762 x BF x D^0.74126 x H^-0.28734 x CL^0.17137 x (BAREA + 1)^-0.00602 x (e^EL)^-0.00209 (cap 50 feet; `vie/cwcalc.f` lines 1215 and 1773).

Some forests use other equations. In SO (forests 4 to 9), WS, NC (forests 1 to 3 and 5), and CA and OC (forests 1 to 5), CWCALC calls subroutine R5CRWD (`vws/r5crwd.f`, the Region 5 equations of Warbington and Levitan) instead of the equation of the map. In R5CRWD, the equations for trees larger than a threshold diameter are those of Warbington and Levitan (Region 5 FIA users guide), the equations for trees from 4.5 feet in height up to the threshold diameter were developed by Dixon, and for trees less than 4.5 feet in height the crown width is a straight line from 0 to the generic intercept (3.5 feet for conifers and 2.5 feet for hardwoods) (`vws/r5crwd.f`).

The map of each variant is shown in the next table: the equation number is the last two digits of the code, and each species is shown with its FIA species code.

*Eastern equations (`ls/cwcalc.f` and `canada/on/cwcalc.f`).* The variables are D, CR and HI, where the Hopkins index is HI = ((100 x ELEV - 887) / 100) + (LAT - 39.54) x 4.0 + (-82.52 - LONG) x 1.25 (the western HI is not used). H and the trees per acre are not used. The forms are shown in equation {4.8.1.12}; every equation is scaled linearly below MIND (5.0 inches) or OMIND (3.0 inches), and has a species cap.

$$
\begin{aligned}
\text{01 (Bechtold):} \quad & CW = a + b\, D \;[+\, c\, D^{2}] \;[+\, d\, CR] \;[+\, e\, HI] \\
\text{02 (Bragg):} \quad & CW = a + b\, D^{c} \\
\text{03 (Ek):} \quad & CW = a + b\, D^{c} \\
\text{04 (Krajicek):} \quad & CW = a + b\, D \\
\text{05 (Smith):} \quad & CW = 3.28084\,\left(a + b \cdot 2.54\, D + c\,(2.54\, D)^{2}\right)
\end{aligned}
\tag{4.8.1.12}
$$

Where:

- CW: Crown width (feet)
- a, b, c, d, e: Coefficients of the species and equation (constants in the CASE of the equation code in the source file); equation 01 has three forms, with the terms for D alone, D and CR, or D, CR and HI
- D: Diameter at breast height (inches)
- CR: Crown ratio (percent)
- HI: Hopkins index of the eastern equations, defined in the text above

Equation 05 (Smith) is coded in metric units and converted to feet.

The forest-grown equation of the species (IWHO = 0) is used by CWIDTH. The open-grown equation (IWHO = 1) is used only by subroutine CCFCAL of the eastern variants to calculate the crown competition factor. The equations of each variant are shown in the next table, where each species is shown with its FIA species code of the forest-grown equation. Species that have no code in the species list of the variant are not shown.

The ON variant has its own copy of the eastern routine, which maps the species through its own table of two-character codes. The crown width of the cover model (subroutine CVCW) is CRWDTH(i), and subroutine CCFCAL of the eastern variants uses the open-grown crown width of subroutine CWCALC with CR of 90 and IWHO of 1 to calculate the crown competition factor, CCFT = 0.001803 x CW^2 x P.

When crown widths have been updated for all tree records, subroutine CWIDTH returns program control to subroutine GRADD. If the cover extension is active, subroutine GRADD next calls CVCNOP to compute new crown area and foliage biomass estimates. CVCNOP will exist as a subroutine if the cover extension is part of the program executable or as an entry point in subroutine EXCOV if the extension is not included in the program executable. And finally, subroutine GRADD calls subroutines PCTILE, DIST, and COMP to update distributions and percentile points for various attributes that have changed during the projection cycle. Subroutine GRADD returns program control back to subroutine TREGRO.

The growth projection portion of the projection cycle is now complete and subroutine TREGRO passes program control back to subroutine FVS which must now complete the end-of-cycle stand and output table updating.

### Auxiliary subroutines

Subroutine DBCHK is used to see if debug output should be written to the output file.

OPDONE, an entry point in subroutine OPFIND, is used to set the year any CRNMULT or FIXCW activities are accomplished.

Subroutine OPFIND is used to find any CRNMULT or FIXCW activities scheduled for the projection cycle.

OPGET, an entry point in subroutine OPFIND, is used to retrieve any CRNMULT or FIXCW activities scheduled for the projection cycle.

Subroutine RANN is used to return a random number in subroutine CROWN: in the Weibull equation for a tree with a diameter of zero, and, through function BACHLO, when missing crown ratios are dubbed in the KT, EM, IE and BC variants.

## Computing stand density and relative density {#sec-computing-stand-density}

FVS describes the density of a stand with several measures that are computed in different subroutines and are used by the growth, mortality, crown, thinning, event monitor and reporting routines. This section describes how each measure is computed. The intent of each measure is described in Dixon (2002), sections 5.2.4.2.4, 7.1.2, 7.3.2 and 7.3.4.

Three kinds of measure are used, and they are different quantities:

- **Crown competition factor (CCF)** (Krajicek et al. 1961) is the percentage of an acre that would be covered by the crowns of the trees if they were open grown; the stand value is the sum of the tree values, and a value of 100 theoretically indicates that crowns just touch in an unthinned, evenly spaced stand (Dixon 2002, section 7.1.2). Variables RELDEN, RELDSP, ATCCF and PCCF are crown competition factor.
- **Stand density index (SDI)** is based on Reineke (1933). FVS computes it by the tree-by-tree summation of Stage (1968), which gives the same result as Reineke's equation with the quadratic mean diameter, and by the summation of Zeide (1983) as simplified by Shaw (2000), which gives the same result as Reineke's equation with the Zeide diameter (Dixon 2002, section 7.3.4). The two methods do not give the same value; the Zeide value is lower, and the difference increases as a stand becomes more uneven aged. Variables SDIBC, SDIAC, SDIMAX, SDIDEF and DR016 are related to SDI.
- **Relative density** in the guide is the measure of Curtis (1982), derived from Reineke's SDI formulation, and the measure of the SILVAH model (Marquis and Ernst 1992), which is used only in the NE variant (Dixon 2002, section 5.2.4.2.4). The point relative density PRDA is also a relative density, defined in the source as the Zeide SDI divided by the maximum SDI of the point.

The source code of subroutine DENSE and the 2018 edition of this guide used the words "relative density by species" for the contribution of each species to stand crown competition factor. In this guide that quantity is called crown competition factor.

### Subroutines involved and their function

**Variables.** The variables of this section are defined in the next table.

```{r density-variables, echo=FALSE}

  ~Variable, ~Definition, ~Units_or_Values,

  "HT(i)", "Total height of record i", "feet",
  "ICR(i)", "Crown ratio of record i", "percent",
  "ISCT(s,1), ISCT(s,2)", "First and last positions of species s in the species-ordered list IND1", "index",
  "IND(k)", "Record numbers in order of decreasing diameter", "index",
  "WK3(i)", "Diameter of record i used for density; DBH(i), or the backdated diameter while calibrating", "inches",
  "WK5(i)", "Squared diameter times trees per acre of record i", "square inches times trees per acre",
  "TPROB", "Total trees per acre", "trees per acre",
  "BA", "Stand basal area", "square feet per acre",
  "RMSQD", "Stand quadratic mean diameter", "inches",
  "DR016", "Reineke diameter calculated with the Zeide method", "inches",
  "AVH", "Average height of the 40 trees per acre with the largest diameters", "feet",
  "RELDSP(s)", "Contribution of species s to stand crown competition factor", "percent of an acre",
  "RELDEN", "Stand crown competition factor", "percent of an acre",
  "RELDM1, OLDBA", "Crown competition factor and basal area for the start of the height increment measurement period while calibrating; for the end of the last cycle in the projection", "percent of an acre; square feet per acre",
  "PCT(i)", "Percentile of record i in the basal area distribution", "percent",
  "PI", "Number of points inventoried, set in INITRE", "points",
  "NONSTK", "Number of non-stockable points inventoried", "points",
  "GROSPC", "Reciprocal of the stockable fraction of the points, 1 / ((PI - NONSTK) / PI), when it was not entered; compensates for non-stockable points", "dimensionless",
  "REGNBK", "Break diameter between understory and overstory trees: 1.000 in AK, 0.499 in CR, 2.999 in all other variants", "inches",
  "PCCF(p), PTPA(p), PTPAA(p), BAAA(p)", "Point p crown competition factor, trees per acre, trees per acre at or above REGNBK, and basal area at or above REGNBK", "as named",
  "OVER(s,p)", "Basal area of species s on point p at or above REGNBK", "square feet per acre",

  "PTBAA(p), PTBALT(i)", "Basal area of point p; basal area of the trees on the point of record i that are larger than record i", "square feet per acre",
  "SDIDEF(s)", "Maximum SDI of species s", "trees per acre",
  "SDIMAX", "Maximum SDI of the stand, weighted by species basal area", "trees per acre",

  "XMAXPT(p)", "Maximum SDI of point p, weighted by species basal area of the point", "trees per acre",
  "BAMAX, LBAMAX", "Maximum basal area; LBAMAX is true when the user entered BAMAX", "square feet per acre; logical",
  "PMSDIL, PMSDIU", "Percent of maximum SDI where density related mortality begins and where the stand reaches maximum density; 55 and 85 in every variant, in percent until subroutine SDICHK divides them by 100", "percent, then proportion",
  "SDIBC, SDIAC", "Stage (Reineke) SDI of the stand before and after thinning", "trees per acre",
  "SDIBC2, SDIAC2", "Zeide SDI of the stand before and after thinning", "trees per acre",

  "DBHSDI", "Minimum diameter in the SDI sum of DENSE and in the SDI based mortality sums of CA, OC, ON, CS, LS and NE; 0 in every variant and no keyword sets it", "inches",
  "LZEIDE, CALCSDI", "True when the Zeide method is used for SDI based mortality and by subroutine SDICHK; default by variant, set by the SDICALC keyword", "logical; text",
  "LBKDEN", "True while subroutine CRATET calls DENSE with backdating of diameters", "logical",

kable(density_variables,
      col.names = c("Variable", "Definition", "Units or values"),
```

**Where the density measures are computed.** Subroutine DENSE computes the stand and point measures and calls subroutines CCFCAL, MBACAL, PCTILE and PTBAL. Subroutine SDICAL computes the maximum SDI; its entry points compute SDI and relative density for a class of trees. The next table lists where they are called.

```{r density-calls, echo=FALSE}
density_calls <- tibble::tribble(
  ~Routine, ~Called_From, ~Condition_or_Purpose,
  "DENSE", "CRATET, in every variant, three times (before the first DGDRIV call; with LBKDEN true; and after the calibration, followed by SDICHK)", "Calibration; LBKDEN = (IDG < 2) for the second call, and false afterwards (ak/cratet.f:104,191-193,652,664)",
  "DENSE", "GRINCR (base/grincr.f:311; canada/bc/grincr.f:307)", "Only when ONTREM(7) > 0, that is, when a thinning occurred",
  "DENSE", "COMCUP (base/comcup.f:203)", "After the tree list is compressed",
  "DENSE", "GRADD (base/gradd.f:192 and 244)", "After mortality and updating of the tree records (following RDPSRT), and after regeneration establishment",
  "SDICAL(0, BTSDIX) and SDICLS", "GRINCR (base/grincr.f:240-241)", "Before-thinning maximum SDI and SDI (SDIBC, SDIBC2)",
  "SDICAL(0, ATSDIX) and SDICLS", "GRINCR (base/grincr.f:322-323)", "After-thinning maximum SDI and SDI (SDIAC, SDIAC2)",
  "SDICLS", "FVS (base/fvs.f:196 and 440-442)", "Before calibration, so that crown ratios dub correctly; and at the end of the projection, where SDIAC is set equal to SDIBC",
  "SDICAL", "MORTS (the morts.f of each variant; vls/morts.f for CS, LS and NE; vwc/morts.f for PN and WC)", "Maximum SDI for mortality",
  "SDICAL", "DGF of AK, CA, CR, EM, HI, IE, NC, OC, OP, PN, TT, UT, WC and WS", "Maximum SDI by point (XMAXPT) with IWHO from the variant; CR, TT and UT call SDICAL(1, SDIMAX) (cr/dgf.f:155; tt/dgf.f:494; ut/dgf.f:499), and CR uses SDIMAX for RELSDI = STDSDI / SDIMAX of the stagnation multiplier (cr/dgf.f:150-160)",
  "SDICAL", "CROWN of AK, CA, HI, NC, OC, OP, PN, WC and WS", "Maximum SDI by point (XMAXPT)",
  "SDICAL", "CRATET (AK only, ak/cratet.f:186); SDICHK (base/sdichk.f:68); CLAUESTB of the climate extension", "Maximum SDI",
  "SDICHK", "CRATET, in every variant, after the last DENSE call", "Reset of the maximum SDI when the initial stand exceeds it"
)

kable(density_calls,
      col.names = c("Routine", "Called from", "Condition or purpose"),
      caption = "Calls of the density routines",
      booktabs = TRUE) %>%
  kable_styling(bootstrap_options = c("striped", "hover", "condensed"),
                full_width = FALSE, font_size = 9) %>%
  column_spec(1, bold = TRUE, width = "8em") %>%
  column_spec(2, width = "18em")
```

Among the calls of subroutine GRINCR at the start of each cycle, the density routines are called in this order: SILFTY, SDICAL and SDICLS (before-thinning values), the saving of the last-cycle values (OLDTPA, OLDAVH, OLDBA, RELDM1 = RELDEN, ORMSQD, ODR016), CUTS, DENSE if a thinning occurred, the saving of the after-thinning values (ATAVD, ATDR016, ATAVH, ATBA, ATCCF = RELDEN, ATTPA), and SDICAL and SDICLS (after-thinning values).

**Subroutine DENSE.** DENSE sums over the live tree records of each species, using the species ordering of ISCT and IND1. All live records are summed; there is no minimum diameter in the sums of TPROB, BA, RMSQD and crown competition factor. The stand values are given in equations {4.9.1.1} to {4.9.1.4}.

$$
TPROB = \sum_{i=1}^{ITRN} PROB_i
\tag{4.9.1.1}
$$

Where:

- TPROB: Total trees per acre of the stand (trees per acre)
- ITRN: Number of live tree records (records)
- PROB_i: Trees per acre represented by record i (trees per acre)

$$
BA = \sum_{i=1}^{ITRN} 0.005454154 \, D_i^{2} \, PROB_i
\tag{4.9.1.2}
$$

Where:

- BA: Stand basal area (square feet per acre)
- ITRN: Number of live tree records (records)
- D_i: Diameter of record i: DBH(i), or the backdated diameter WK3(i) in the first pass of a backdating call (inches)
- PROB_i: Trees per acre represented by record i (trees per acre)

$$
RMSQD = \sqrt{\frac{\sum_{i=1}^{ITRN} D_i^{2} \, PROB_i}{TPROB}}
\tag{4.9.1.3}
$$

Where:

- RMSQD: Quadratic mean diameter of the stand (inches)
- ITRN: Number of live tree records (records)
- D_i: Diameter of record i: DBH(i), or the backdated diameter WK3(i) in the first pass of a backdating call (inches)
- PROB_i: Trees per acre represented by record i (trees per acre)
- TPROB: Total trees per acre of the stand (trees per acre)

$$
DR016 = \left(\frac{\sum_{i=1,\, D_i \ge DBHSDI}^{ITRN} PROB_i \, D_i^{1.605}}{TPROB}\right)^{1/1.605}
\tag{4.9.1.4}
$$

Where:

- DR016: Reineke diameter calculated with the Zeide method (inches)
- ITRN: Number of live tree records (records)
- D_i: Diameter of record i: DBH(i), or the backdated diameter WK3(i) in the first pass of a backdating call (inches)
- DBHSDI: Minimum diameter in the sum, 0 in every variant (inches)
- PROB_i: Trees per acre represented by record i (trees per acre)
- TPROB: Total trees per acre of the stand (trees per acre)

The stand crown competition factor is the sum of the tree values from subroutine CCFCAL, as shown in equation {4.9.1.5}. DENSE calls CCFCAL with MODE = 1 and LTHIN false.

$$
\begin{aligned} RELDEN &= \sum_{s} RELDSP_s \\ RELDSP_s &= \sum_{i \in s} CCF_i \end{aligned}
\tag{4.9.1.5}
$$

Where:

- RELDEN: Stand crown competition factor (percent)
- CCF_i: Crown competition factor of record i from subroutine CCFCAL, which already includes the trees per acre of the record (percent)

The point values are the sums of equations {4.9.1.6} to {4.9.1.10}, where p is the point of the record. They are not recomputed on the second pass of a backdating call. The values with a diameter limit use only records with D at or above REGNBK.

$$
PCCF_p = \sum_{i \in p} CCF_i \, \frac{PI}{GROSPC}
\tag{4.9.1.6}
$$

Where:

- PCCF_p: Crown competition factor of point p (percent)
- CCF_i: Crown competition factor of record i from subroutine CCFCAL, which already includes the trees per acre of the record (percent)
- PI: Number of points inventoried (points)
- GROSPC: Reciprocal of the stockable fraction of the points (dimensionless)

$$
PTPA_p = \sum_{i \in p} PROB_i \, \frac{PI}{GROSPC}
\tag{4.9.1.7}
$$

Where:

- PTPA_p: Trees per acre of point p (trees per acre)
- PROB_i: Trees per acre represented by record i (trees per acre)
- PI: Number of points inventoried (points)
- GROSPC: Reciprocal of the stockable fraction of the points (dimensionless)

$$
\begin{aligned} BAAA_p &= \sum_{i \in p,\, D_i \ge REGNBK} BA_i \, \frac{PI}{GROSPC} \\ BA_i &= 0.005454154 \, D_i^{2} \, PROB_i \end{aligned}
\tag{4.9.1.8}
$$

Where:

- BAAA_p: Basal area of point p in trees at or above REGNBK (square feet per acre)
- D_i: Diameter of record i: DBH(i), or the backdated diameter WK3(i) in the first pass of a backdating call (inches)
- PROB_i: Trees per acre represented by record i (trees per acre)
- REGNBK: Break diameter between understory and overstory trees: 1.000 in AK, 0.499 in CR and 2.999 in the other variants (inches)
- PI: Number of points inventoried (points)
- GROSPC: Reciprocal of the stockable fraction of the points (dimensionless)

$$
PTPAA_p = \sum_{i \in p,\, D_i \ge REGNBK} PROB_i \, \frac{PI}{GROSPC}
\tag{4.9.1.9}
$$

Where:

- PTPAA_p: Trees per acre of point p at or above REGNBK (trees per acre)
- D_i: Diameter of record i: DBH(i), or the backdated diameter WK3(i) in the first pass of a backdating call (inches)
- PROB_i: Trees per acre represented by record i (trees per acre)
- REGNBK: Break diameter between understory and overstory trees: 1.000 in AK, 0.499 in CR and 2.999 in the other variants (inches)
- PI: Number of points inventoried (points)
- GROSPC: Reciprocal of the stockable fraction of the points (dimensionless)

$$
PRDA_p = \sum_{i \in p,\, D_i \ge REGNBK} \frac{PROB_i \left(D_i / 10\right)^{1.605} \, PI / GROSPC}{XMAXPT_p}
\tag{4.9.1.10}
$$

Where:

- PRDA_p: Point relative density: Zeide SDI of the trees of point p at or above REGNBK divided by the maximum SDI of the point
- D_i: Diameter of record i: DBH(i), or the backdated diameter WK3(i) in the first pass of a backdating call (inches)
- PROB_i: Trees per acre represented by record i (trees per acre)
- REGNBK: Break diameter between understory and overstory trees: 1.000 in AK, 0.499 in CR and 2.999 in the other variants (inches)
- PI: Number of points inventoried (points)
- GROSPC: Reciprocal of the stockable fraction of the points (dimensionless)
- XMAXPT_p: Maximum SDI of point p from subroutine SDICAL (trees per acre); the term is added only when it is greater than 0

The average height of the dominants, AVH, is the average height of the 40 trees per acre with the largest diameters. DENSE walks IND from the largest diameter, adds the trees per acre of each record, limits the last record so that the cumulative trees per acre is 40, and averages the heights weighted by the trees per acre used. DENSE calls subroutine MBACAL to identify the site species, the species with the most basal area.

**Backdating.** While calibrating (LBKDEN true, which CRATET sets when IDG is less than 2), DENSE estimates the density at the start of the diameter increment measurement period. The diameters are backdated with equation {4.9.1.11}. BAGR is the average of R_i over the records with DG(i) of 0 or more and an increment G_i not above D_i; it replaces R_i for a record with DG(i) below 0 or R_i of 0 or less. Records from IREC2 to MAXTRE keep their diameter in WK3, and records with IMC = 9 are given a diameter of 0.

$$
\begin{aligned} WK3_i &= \sqrt{D_i^{2} R_i} \\ R_i &= 1 - \frac{2 D_i G_i - G_i^{2}}{D_i^{2}} \end{aligned}
\tag{4.9.1.11}
$$

Where:

- WK3_i: Backdated diameter of record i (inches)
- D_i: Current diameter of record i, DBH(i) (inches)
- G_i: Diameter increment of record i, DG(i), divided by the bark ratio BRATIO(species, DBH, HT) when IDG is not 1, and then limited to D_i (inches)

The species loop is run twice. The first pass uses WK3 and gives RELDM1 and OLDBA; the percentile PCT is computed from that pass, and the point values of equations {4.9.1.6} to {4.9.1.10} are those of the backdated stand. The second pass uses the current diameters and gives RELDEN, BA, RMSQD and DR016. The values are then reassigned with equation {4.9.1.12}, where the subscripts 1 and 2 of C and B are the first and second pass.

$$
\begin{aligned} RAT &= \frac{FINTH}{FINT} \\ RELDM1 &= RAT \left(C_{2} - C_{1}\right) + C_{1} \\ RELDEN &= C_{1} \\ OLDBA &= RAT \left(B_{2} - B_{1}\right) + B_{1} \\ BA &= B_{1} \end{aligned}
\tag{4.9.1.12}
$$

Where:

- RELDM1: Stand crown competition factor at the start of the height increment measurement period (percent)
- RELDEN: Stand crown competition factor at the start of the diameter increment measurement period (percent)
- OLDBA: Stand basal area at the start of the height increment measurement period (square feet per acre)
- BA: Stand basal area at the start of the diameter increment measurement period (square feet per acre)
- FINTH: Measurement period for small-tree height growth (years)
- FINT: Length of the current cycle, as stored in PLOT.F77 (years)
- C_{1}, C_{2}: Stand crown competition factor of the first pass (backdated diameters) and of the second pass (current diameters) (percent)
- B_{1}, B_{2}: Stand basal area of the first pass (backdated diameters) and of the second pass (current diameters) (square feet per acre)

**Percentile of the basal area distribution.** Subroutine DENSE calls subroutine PCTILE with the array IND (record numbers in order of decreasing diameter) and the vector WK5 = D^2 P. PCTILE accumulates WK5 from the smallest record up to each record, divides by the total divided by 100, and sets the largest record to 100, as shown in equation {4.9.1.13}. PCT(i) is therefore the percentage of the basal area in record i and all records that are the same size or smaller (Dixon 2002, section 7.1.2). With one record PCT is 100. PCTILE returns before dividing if the total is 0 or less.

$$
\begin{aligned} PCT_{IND(k)} &= 100 \, \frac{\sum_{j=k}^{ITRN} WK5_{IND(j)}}{\sum_{j=1}^{ITRN} WK5_{IND(j)}} \\ WK5_i &= D_i^{2} \, PROB_i \end{aligned}
\tag{4.9.1.13}
$$

Where:

- PCT_{IND(k)}: Percentile in the basal area distribution of the record at position k of IND, where position 1 is the largest diameter (percent)
- IND(j): Record number at position j of IND, in order of decreasing diameter
- D_i: Diameter at breast height of record i, DBH(i) (inches)
- PROB_i: Trees per acre represented by record i (trees per acre)
- ITRN: Number of live tree records (records)

The basal area in larger trees used by the growth equations is BAL = (1 - PCT/100) x BA, as described with each equation in the growth section.

**Point basal area in larger trees.** Subroutine PTBAL is called from DENSE. In the CS, LS, NE and ON variants it sets PTBALT and PTBAA to 0. In all other variants, for each point it walks the records of the point from the largest diameter down and assigns, as shown in equations {4.9.1.14} and {4.9.1.15}, the basal area accumulated before the record is added, so that PTBALT(i) does not include record i.

$$
PTBALT_{i_m} = \sum_{n=1}^{m-1} 0.005454154 \, WK5_{i_n} \, \frac{PI}{GROSPC}
\tag{4.9.1.14}
$$

Where:

- PTBALT_{i_m}: Basal area of the larger trees on the point of record i_m, where i_m is the record at position m among the records of its point in order of decreasing diameter (square feet per acre)
- WK5_{i_n}: Squared diameter times trees per acre of record i_n (square inches times trees per acre)
- PI: Number of points inventoried (points)
- GROSPC: Reciprocal of the stockable fraction of the points (dimensionless)

$$
PTBAA_p = \sum_{n=1}^{N_p} 0.005454154 \, WK5_{i_n} \, \frac{PI}{GROSPC}
\tag{4.9.1.15}
$$

Where:

- PTBAA_p: Basal area of point p (square feet per acre)
- N_p: Number of records on point p (records)
- WK5_{i_n}: Squared diameter times trees per acre of record i_n, the record at position n among the records of point p (square inches times trees per acre)
- PI: Number of points inventoried (points)
- GROSPC: Reciprocal of the stockable fraction of the points (dimensionless)

**Stockable area.** INITRE computes GROSPC from the number of points and the number of non-stockable points when GROSPC is negative, that is, not entered (GROSPC = (PI - NONSTK) / PI, limited to 1), and then replaces it with its reciprocal (vbase/initre.f, near lines 350 to 381). When the value is not 1, FVS prints that stand attributes are calculated per acre of stockable area and that the values in the summary table are multiplied by the stockable fraction. Stand density index, crown competition factor and crown cover are based on stockable area (Dixon 2002, section 5.5.2.2).

**Crown competition factor of a tree, subroutine CCFCAL.** CCFCAL(ISPC, D, H, JCR, P, LTHIN, CCFT, CRWDTH, MODE) returns the crown competition factor CCFT of a record in MODE 1, already multiplied by the trees per acre P, and, in some variants, a crown width in MODE 2, which DENSE does not use. The source file differs by variant (see the next table). CS, LS, NE, ON and SN use the file of LS; OC uses the file of CA; OP uses the file of PN. The variables that are not defined above are D (diameter, inches), H (total height, feet) and JCR (crown ratio, percent). The forms are given once, in equations {4.9.1.16} to {4.9.1.20}, and the table lists the form, the break diameter DB and the source of each species. The coefficient arrays RD1, RD2, RD3, RDA and RDB are in the files named in the table.

$$
CCF = \begin{cases} RD1 + RD2 \, D + RD3 \, D^{2} & D \ge DB \\ RDA \, D^{RDB} & 0.1 < D < DB \\ 0.001 & D \le 0.1 \end{cases}
\tag{4.9.1.16}
$$

Where:

- CCF: Crown competition factor of the record per tree, before multiplying by PROB (percent)
- D: Diameter at breast height of the record, DBH(i) (inches)
- DB: Break diameter of the species in the variant table (inches)
- RD1, RD2, RD3, RDA, RDB: Coefficients of the species, arrays of the file named in the table

$$
CCF = \begin{cases} RD1 + RD2 \, D + RD3 \, D^{2} & D \ge DB \\ D \left(RD1 + RD2 + RD3\right) & D < DB \end{cases}
\tag{4.9.1.17}
$$

Where:

- CCF: Crown competition factor of the record per tree, before multiplying by PROB (percent)
- D: Diameter at breast height of the record, DBH(i) (inches)
- DB: Break diameter of the species in the variant table (inches)
- RD1, RD2, RD3: Coefficients of the species, arrays of the file named in the table

$$
CCF = 0.001803 \, CW^{2}
\tag{4.9.1.18}
$$

Where:

- CCF: Crown competition factor of the record per tree, before multiplying by PROB (percent)
- CW: Crown width of the record from R5CRWD, R6CRWD or CWCALC (feet)

$$
\begin{aligned} MCW &= \begin{cases} B1 + B2 \, D & EQMAP = 1 \\ 3.28 \, B1 \left(2.54 \, D\right)^{B2} & EQMAP = 2 \end{cases} \\ CCF &= 100 \, \frac{3.14159 \left(MCW / 2\right)^{2}}{43560} \end{aligned}
\tag{4.9.1.19}
$$

Where:

- CCF: Crown competition factor of the record per tree, before multiplying by PROB (percent)
- D: Diameter at breast height of the record, DBH(i) (inches)
- B1, B2: Coefficients of the species, arrays B1 and B2 of ak/ccfcal.f
- EQMAP: Equation form of the species, array EQMAP of ak/ccfcal.f

$$
CCF = 0.001803 \left(RD1 + RD2 \, D\right)^{2} \qquad (D \ge 1.0)
\tag{4.9.1.20}
$$

Where:

- CCF: Crown competition factor of the record per tree, before multiplying by PROB (percent)
- D: Diameter at breast height of the record, DBH(i) (inches)
- RD1, RD2: Coefficients of the species, arrays RD1 and RD2 of ws/ccfcal.f

Every form is multiplied by PROB after it is evaluated. In form A, CCF is set to 0.001 at D of 0.1 or less only where the table does not say "without the 0.001 floor". In form C, CW is the crown width in feet: from R5CRWD or R6CRWD, or from CWCALC with a crown ratio of 90 in the variants that use the file of LS. In AK, the result of equation {4.9.1.19} is also set to 0.001 for D of 0.1 or less. Form E (WS) applies for D at or above 1.0; below 1.0 WS uses form A with DB = 1.0.


**Subroutine SDICAL: maximum SDI.** The maximum SDI of the stand is the average of the species maximums SDIDEF weighted by the basal area of each species, as shown in equations {4.9.1.21} and {4.9.1.22} (Dixon 2002, equation 7.3.2.1.1). The sums use the live records (index below IREC2) with the basal area 0.0054542 D^2 P. When IWHO is 1 during calibration, recently dead records (IMC = 7) are also included, with their trees per acre divided by FINT / FINTM; this is used by the stagnation calculation of the CR, TT and UT variants. The maximum SDI of each point, XMAXPT, is the same average of the species basal area on the point; it equals the stand value when the point has no basal area.

$$
SDIMAX = \frac{\sum_{s} SDIDEF_s \, BAXSP_s}{\sum_{s} BAXSP_s}
\tag{4.9.1.21}
$$

Where:

- SDIMAX: Maximum SDI of the stand, set to 1 when the stand has no basal area (trees per acre)
- SDIDEF_s: Maximum SDI of species s (trees per acre)
- BAXSP_s: Basal area of species s, the sum over live records of species s of 0.0054542 D^2 PROB (square feet per acre)

$$
XMAXPT_p = \frac{\sum_{s} SDIDEF_s \, BAXPSP_{s,p}}{\sum_{s} BAXPSP_{s,p}}
\tag{4.9.1.22}
$$

Where:

- XMAXPT_p: Maximum SDI of point p; equal to SDIMAX when the point has no basal area (trees per acre)
- SDIDEF_s: Maximum SDI of species s (trees per acre)
- BAXPSP_{s,p}: Basal area of species s on point p, the sum over live records of the species on the point of 0.0054542 D^2 PROB (square feet per acre)

SDICAL then adjusts the basal area maximum and the SDI maximum so that they correspond, as shown in equation {4.9.1.23}. Subroutine CLMAXDEN, which is part of the climate extension, then changes the value returned.

$$
\begin{aligned} BAMAX &= SDIMAX \times 0.5454154 \times PMSDIU && (LBAMAX \text{ false}) \\ SDIMAX &= \frac{BAMAX}{0.5454154 \times TEM} && (LBAMAX \text{ true}) \end{aligned}
\tag{4.9.1.23}
$$

Where:

- BAMAX: Maximum basal area (square feet per acre)
- SDIMAX: Maximum SDI of the stand; in the second line it replaces the species weighted value of equation {4.9.1.21} (trees per acre)
- PMSDIU: Proportion of maximum SDI at which the stand reaches maximum density, a proportion once SDICHK has divided it by 100
- TEM: PMSDIU divided by 100 when PMSDIU is above 1, otherwise PMSDIU
- LBAMAX: True when the user entered BAMAX (logical)

With a user BAMAX, the value returned replaces the species weighted value; the point values XMAXPT still use the species values SDIDEF. Dixon (2002) equation 7.3.2.2.1 gives SDImax = BAmax / 0.54542; the code also divides by TEM (0.85 by default).

**SDI of a class of trees, entry SDICLS.** SDICLS(JSPEC, DLO, DHI, IWHO, SDIC, SDIC2, A, B, JPNUM) returns the Stage SDI and the Zeide SDI of the live records of a species (0 for all, a negative number for a species group), in a diameter range from DLO up to but not including DHI, for one point (JPNUM greater than 0) or the stand (0). IWHO = 1 uses PROB and IWHO = 2 uses WK4, the trees per acre removed by a thinning. The Stage parameters A and B are computed from all live records at or above DBHSTAGE, as shown in equation {4.9.1.24}, together with the Stage sum; the Zeide sum is in equation {4.9.1.25}. For a point, the trees per acre are multiplied by PI minus NONSTK.



$$
\begin{aligned} SDIC &= \sum_{D_i \ge DBHSTAGE} \left(A + B \, D_i^{2}\right) T_i \\ A &= 10^{-1.605} \left(1 - \frac{1.605}{2}\right) QMD_S^{1.605} \\ B &= 10^{-1.605} \, \frac{1.605}{2} \, QMD_S^{1.605 - 2} \end{aligned}
\tag{4.9.1.24}
$$

Where:

- SDIC: Stage (Reineke) SDI of the class of trees, SDIBC or SDIAC for the stand (trees per acre)
- D_i: Diameter at breast height of record i, DBH(i) (inches)
- DBHSTAGE: Minimum diameter of the sum, set with the SDICALC keyword, default 0 (inches)
- T_i: Trees per acre of record i, PROB(i) when IWHO is 1 or WK4(i) when IWHO is 2 (trees per acre)
- QMD_S: Quadratic mean diameter of all live records at or above DBHSTAGE (inches)

$$
SDIC2 = \sum_{D_i \ge DBHZEIDE} T_i \left(\frac{D_i}{10}\right)^{1.605}
\tag{4.9.1.25}
$$

Where:

- SDIC2: Zeide SDI of the class of trees, SDIBC2 or SDIAC2 for the stand (trees per acre)
- D_i: Diameter at breast height of record i, DBH(i) (inches)
- DBHZEIDE: Minimum diameter of the sum, set with the SDICALC keyword, default 0 (inches)
- T_i: Trees per acre of record i, PROB(i) when IWHO is 1 or WK4(i) when IWHO is 2 (trees per acre)

When a species or a species group is specified (JSPEC not 0), records of species flagged in the array LEAVESP (the leave species of CONTRL.F77, set in vbase/cuts.f:1477 and 1488) are not included; JSPEC = 0 includes all live records. SDIC is SDIBC or SDIAC (Stage method; Dixon 2002, equation 7.3.2.1.2) and SDIC2 is SDIBC2 or SDIAC2 (Zeide method; Dixon 2002, equation 7.3.2.1.3).

The default method used for SDI based mortality and for the SDI used by subroutine SDICHK, LZEIDE, is set by variant in GRINIT and by region in SITSET (when the SDICALC keyword has not been used), as shown in the next table. The SDICALC keyword sets DBHSTAGE (field 1), DBHZEIDE (field 2) and the method (field 3 of 1 or more gives Zeide, otherwise Reineke).

```{r lzeide-defaults, echo=FALSE}
lzeide_defaults <- tibble::tribble(
  ~Variants, ~LZEIDE_Default, ~Region_Override,
  "AK, CS, LS, NE, CR, SN, TT, UT, WS", "TRUE", "None",
  "CA", "TRUE", "FALSE for IFOR of 6 or more (ca/sitset.f:94-95)",
  "NC", "TRUE", "FALSE for IFOR 4 or 7 (nc/sitset.f:72-73)",
  "SO", "TRUE", "FALSE for IFOR of 3 or less, or 10 (so/sitset.f:81-82)",
  "CI", "TRUE", "FALSE for IFOR below 2 (ci/sitset.f:153)",
  "BM, EC, EM, HI, IE, KT, OC, OP, PN, WC, BC, ON", "FALSE", "None in sitset.f"
)

kable(lzeide_defaults,
      col.names = c("Variants", "LZEIDE default (grinit.f)", "Region override when CALCSDI is blank"),
      caption = "Default SDI method by variant",
      booktabs = TRUE) %>%
  kable_styling(bootstrap_options = c("striped", "hover", "condensed"),
                full_width = FALSE, font_size = 9) %>%
  column_spec(1, bold = TRUE, width = "14em")
```

**Subroutine SDICHK.** CRATET calls SDICHK after the last DENSE call of the calibration. It divides PMSDIL and PMSDIU by 100, calls SDICAL to get SDIMAX, and compares the initial trees per acre with the upper limit, as shown in equation {4.9.1.26} (Dixon 2002, section 7.3.2.1). The stand diameter of the comparison, D0, is RMSQD, or DR016 when LZEIDE is true. If the initial TPROB is more than UPMAX times the maximum trees per acre at the stand diameter, all species maximums SDIDEF are set to one value, a warning is written, and LFIXSD is set true. LFIXSD is not used elsewhere except by PUTSTD and GETSTD.

$$
\begin{aligned} CONST &= \frac{SDIMAX}{0.02483133} \\ TEMMAX &= CONST \cdot D0^{-1.605} \\ UPMAX &= \min\left(1,\; PMSDIU + 0.05\right) \\ \text{if } TPROB &> UPMAX \cdot TEMMAX: \\ CONST &= \frac{\exp\left[\ln(TPROB + 1) + 1.605 \ln(D0)\right]}{PMSDIU}, \qquad SDIDEF_s = 0.02483133 \cdot CONST \end{aligned}
\tag{4.9.1.26}
$$

Where:

- SDIMAX: Maximum SDI of the stand from SDICAL (trees per acre)
- D0: Stand diameter of the comparison: RMSQD, or DR016 when LZEIDE is true (inches)
- TPROB: Total trees per acre of the stand (trees per acre)
- PMSDIU: Proportion of maximum SDI at which the stand reaches maximum density, after the division by 100
- SDIDEF_s: Maximum SDI of species s, the same value for all species after the reset (trees per acre)

D0 has no minimum in this comparison; a copy of the diameter with a minimum of 0.3, and the maximum trees per acre at that diameter limited to 35000, are used only in the printed warning.

**Maximum SDI and BAMAX by variant.** SITSET sets SDIDEF and BAMAX for the values that were not entered with the SDIMAX and BAMAX keywords. The SDIMAX keyword (field 2) sets SDIDEF for a species, a species group or all species, and sets MAXSDI to 1; fields 3 and 4 are not used; field 5 sets PMSDIL (not below 10); field 6 sets PMSDIU (not above 95); and field 7 is the stagnation indicator ISTAGF in CR, TT and UT. The BAMAX keyword sets BAMAX and LBAMAX, and the SETSITE keyword does the same in GRINCR with its field 2 (BAMAX) and field 6 (SDIDEF); neither base/grincr.f nor canada/bc/grincr.f contains a call to SITSET. The next table gives the source of the values of SITSET.

In BM, EC, HI, OP, PN and WC, and in CA and OC (IFOR of 6 or more), NC (IFOR 4 or 7) and SO (IFOR 3 or less, or 10), the maximum SDI of the species of the ecological class code is first set from ECOCLS (RSDI, limited to the value FORMAX of the variant: 850 in BM, CA, NC, OC and SO; 900 in EC; 950 in HI, OP and PN; FMSDI(IFOR) in WC), before the table values are applied to the species that are still not set. SITSET changes BAMAX only where the table says so; where LBAMAX is false, SDICAL sets BAMAX again from SDIMAX each time it is called (equation {4.9.1.23}). When the ORGANON variables RVARS(3 to 5) and MSDI_1 to MSDI_3 are 0, OC and OP set them from SDIDEF of three species (OC: species 7, 4 and 18; OP: species 16, 3 and 19 for RVARS and 16, 15 and 3 for MSDI_1 to MSDI_3), as listed in oc/sitset.f:327-342 and op/sitset.f:325-340.

**Relative density of a class of trees.** Entry RDCLS computes the relative density of Curtis (1982) with the summation of Lu et al. (2017), shown in equation {4.9.1.27}, for the records at or above DBHSTAGE (Dixon 2002, equation 5.2.4.2.4.1). Entries RDCLS2 and RDSLTR compute the SILVAH relative density (Marquis and Ernst 1992), shown in equation {4.9.1.28}; they are available only in NE and use records with a diameter of 1.0 inch or more. Entry CCCLS computes the percent canopy cover, shown in equation {4.9.1.29}. Entry SILFTY assigns the SILVAH forest type (0 to 5) in NE; the types are those defined in Dixon (2002), section 5.2.4.2.4, with the thresholds 0.65, 0.50 and 0.25 of basal area.

$$
\begin{aligned} RD &= \sum_{D_i \ge DBHSTAGE} \left(a + b \, D_i^{2}\right) T_i \\ a &= \frac{0.25 \, \pi}{24^{2}} \, QMD^{1.5}, \qquad b = \frac{0.75 \, \pi}{24^{2}} \, QMD^{-0.5} \end{aligned}
\tag{4.9.1.27}
$$

Where:

- RD: Relative density of Curtis (1982) of the class of trees
- D_i: Diameter at breast height of record i, DBH(i) (inches)
- DBHSTAGE: Minimum diameter included in the sum, set with the SDICALC keyword (inches)
- T_i: Trees per acre of record i, PROB(i) when IWHO is 1 or WK4(i) when IWHO is 2 (trees per acre)
- QMD: Quadratic mean diameter of all live records at or above DBHSTAGE (inches)

$$
RD_{S} = \sum_{i} \max\left[0,\; \left(a_g + b_g \, D_i + c_g \, D_i^{2}\right) T_i\right] \qquad (D_i \ge 1.0)
\tag{4.9.1.28}
$$

Where:

- RD_{S}: Relative density of SILVAH (Marquis and Ernst 1992) of the class of trees
- D_i: Diameter at breast height of record i, DBH(i) (inches)
- a_g, b_g, c_g: Coefficients of the species group g of the record, given by the array MAPNE of vbase/sdical.f: group 1 0.0033033, 0.020426, 0.0006776; group 2 -0.027142, 0.024257, 0.0015225; group 3 -0.0027935, 0.0058959, 0.0047289
- T_i: Trees per acre of record i, PROB(i) when IWHO is 1 or WK4(i) when IWHO is 2 (trees per acre)

$$
\begin{aligned} CCCL &= 100 \left[1 - \exp\left(-\min\left(86,\; CCCOEF \cdot CCCL_{0}\right)\right)\right] \\ CCCL_{0} &= 100 \, \frac{0.785398 \, CRA}{43560} \\ CRA &= \sum_{i} CW_i^{2} \, T_i \end{aligned}
\tag{4.9.1.29}
$$

Where:

- CCCL: Percent canopy cover of the class of trees (percent)
- CCCOEF: Canopy cover overlap coefficient, set with the CCADJ keyword
- CW_i: Crown width of record i, CRWDTH(i) (feet)
- T_i: Trees per acre of record i, PROB(i) when IWHO is 1 or WK4(i) when IWHO is 2 (trees per acre)

The limit of 86 on the exponent avoids a numerical underflow (source comment).

**Relative density of the stand.** The event monitor variables BRDEN and ARDEN are the relative density of Curtis (1982) of the stand before and after a thinning (Dixon 2002, section 5.5.2.2). Subroutine EVTSTV computes them from the stand values of DENSE, as shown in equation {4.9.1.30}, and sets them to 0 when RMSQD is 0 (vbase/evtstv.f:270,281,288-292 and 509,512,535-537); it does not use entry RDCLS.

$$
BRDEN, \; ARDEN = \frac{BA / GROSPC}{\sqrt{RMSQD}}
\tag{4.9.1.30}
$$

Where:

- BRDEN, ARDEN: Relative density of Curtis (1982) of the stand before and after a thinning
- BA: Stand basal area before or after the thinning, equation {4.9.1.2} (square feet per acre)
- GROSPC: Reciprocal of the stockable fraction of the points (dimensionless)
- RMSQD: Quadratic mean diameter of the stand before or after the thinning, equation {4.9.1.3} (inches)

The event monitor variables BRDEN2 and ARDEN2 are the relative density of SILVAH of the stand before and after a thinning. EVTSTV computes them with entry RDCLS2 for all species and all diameters, as shown in equation {4.9.1.31} (vbase/evtstv.f:294-295 and 562-563). RDCLS2 returns 0 outside the NE variant.

$$
BRDEN2, \; ARDEN2 = \frac{RD_{S}}{GROSPC}
\tag{4.9.1.31}
$$

Where:

- BRDEN2, ARDEN2: Relative density of SILVAH of the stand before and after a thinning
- RD_{S}: Relative density of SILVAH of all live records of the stand at or above 1.0 inch, equation {4.9.1.28}
- GROSPC: Reciprocal of the stockable fraction of the points (dimensionless)

The ratio of the stand SDI to the maximum SDI is the column RDSDI of the FVS_Summary2 database table. The SDI of the summary table is the Zeide SDI when LZEIDE is true and the Stage SDI otherwise, rounded to an integer (vbase/disply.f:325,334,336-338). RDSDI is that integer divided by the maximum SDI before thinning, as shown in equation {4.9.1.32}; the records that report the after-thinning values use the after-thinning SDI as the numerator and the same denominator (vdbsqlite/dbssumry.f:301,509,528). The crown routines use the ratio of SDIAC to the maximum SDI of each species, RELSDI, which is described in [Computing crown ratio change and crown width](#sec-computing-crown-ratio-change-and-crown-width).

$$
\begin{aligned} RDSDI &= \frac{ISDI}{BTSDIX} \\ ISDI &= INT\left(\frac{SDI}{GROSPC} + 0.5\right) \end{aligned}
\tag{4.9.1.32}
$$

Where:

- RDSDI: Ratio of the SDI of the summary table to the maximum SDI before thinning
- ISDI: SDI of the summary table (trees per acre)
- BTSDIX: Maximum SDI of the stand before thinning, from SDICAL in GRINCR (trees per acre)
- SDI: SDIBC2 or SDIBC (before thinning), or SDIAC2 or SDIAC (after thinning), as described in the text; SDIBC2 and SDIAC2 when LZEIDE is true (trees per acre)
- GROSPC: Reciprocal of the stockable fraction of the points (dimensionless)

**Diameter limit of the SDI based mortality sums.** The mortality routines exclude trees below a diameter limit from the SDI sums, as shown in the next table.

```{r sdi-mortality-limit, echo=FALSE}
  "CA, OC, ON, CS, LS, NE", "DBHSDI", "ca/morts.f:203,567; oc/morts.f:208,597; canada/on/morts.f:255,656; vls/morts.f:203,571"
)
```

### Auxiliary subroutines

Subroutine DBCHK is used to see if debug output should be written to the output file.

Subroutine CCFCAL is used by subroutine DENSE to compute the crown competition factor of each tree record. It calls subroutines R5CRWD, R6CRWD or CWCALC in the variants that compute crown width.

Subroutine MBACAL is used by subroutine DENSE to identify the species with the most basal area.

Subroutine PCTILE is used by subroutine DENSE to compute the percentile of each tree record in the basal area distribution.

Subroutine PTBAL is used by subroutine DENSE to compute the point basal area and the basal area in larger trees on the point.

Subroutine CLMAXDEN is used by subroutine SDICAL to change the maximum SDI when the climate extension is active.

Subroutine SDICHK is used to reset the maximum SDI when the initial stand is denser than the upper limit of density related mortality.

## End-Of-Cycle Updating of stand and output information

FVS has several tasks to accomplish at the end of a projection cycle. Output tables must be updated, files used in post-processing programs may need to be written, and stand age might need to be reset.

### Subroutines involved and their function

Subroutine FVS calls subroutine EXTREE to assign values to the output arrays for example trees. Subscripts to trees used for printing in the output tables are carried in array INS(i), i=1,6, and passed in the CONTRL labeled COMMON block. The INS(i) array is loaded in subroutine DIST.

Subroutine FVS then calls subroutine DISPLY to write the end-of-cycle stand and tree statistics to the stand composition, sample tree, and summary statistics tables. For cycles after the inventory, DISPLY also calls subroutines DBSSUMRY2 and DBSCARBBIOSUMRY to write the summary statistics and carbon and biomass summary to the output database when database output has been requested. The scalar variable ICL6 is used for various purposes in FVS and is carried in the CONTRL labeled COMMON block. Subroutine DISPLY checks the value of ICL6 to know if the projection is complete (ICL6 < 0) or not (ICL6 > 0). Processing once the projection is complete is discussed in [Projection Summarization Phase](#sec-projection-summarization-phase).

Subroutine FVS calls subroutine RESAGE to reset the stand age if any RESETAGE keyword records were specified by the user. Users may want to reset the stand age when regeneration or other management activities occur that significantly change the composition of the stand.

Subroutine FVS next calls MISPRT to write end-of-cycle values to dwarf mistletoe summary tables. MISPRT will exist as a subroutine if the dwarf mistletoe extension is part of the program executable, or as an entry point in subroutine EXMIST if the dwarf mistletoe extension in not part of the program executable.

Code segments that write summary output for other insect and disease extensions are called next. These code segments are RDPR for the western root disease model and BRPR for the blister rust model. RDPR and BRPR will exist as subroutines if the extension is part of the program executable or as an entry point in the corresponding externals subroutine if it is not.

Calls to subroutines that write end-of-cycle tree list information for the projection cycle come next. Subroutine PRTRLS is called to print tree list if it was requested with the TREELIST keyword record, and subroutine DBS_FIAVBC_TRLS writes the FIA-VBC tree list table to the output database when that table has been requested. Subroutine FVSSTD is called to write information needed by the FVSStand post-processing program if requested with the FVSSTAND keyword record.

Processing of the projection cycle is now complete. Subroutine FVS compares ICYC with NCYC. If this was not the last cycle of the projection, the restart code is cleared, the cycle number gets incremented, and the process starts over with the call to subroutine TREGRO as outlined in [Event monitor and harvest](#sec-event-monitor-and-harvest). If it was the last cycle, subroutine FVS processes stop point -1, which signals that stopping can no longer continue for this stand (see [Stop/restart and the FVS API](#sec-stop-restart-and-the-fvs-api)), increments ICYC, sets ICL6 to -99 to indicate the projection is complete, calls DISPLY for the final time, and enters the projection summarization phase.

### Auxiliary subroutines

Subroutine FORTYP is used to compute the FIA forest type based on stand stocking levels.

OPDONE, an entry point in subroutine OPFIND, is used to set the year any RESETAGE, FVSSTAND, or TREELIST activities are accomplished.

Subroutine OPFIND is used to find any RESETAGE, FVSSTAND, or TREELIST activities scheduled for the projection cycle.

OPGET, an entry point in subroutine OPFIND, is used to retrieve any RESETAGE, FVSSTAND, or TREELIST activities scheduled for the projection cycle.

Subroutine SDICAL is called to compute the end-of-cycle SDI maximum.

# Projection Summarization Phase {#sec-projection-summarization-phase}

When all projection cycles have been completed, FVS enters the projection summarization phase. The final output reports must be produced, another projection of the same stand, or a different stand, may be called for, or the program might be directed to stop.
